title: Activate the existing MinIO document repository for local uploads

evidence.uncertainty: The repository and settings selection already exist, but the active backend process and live object-store behavior must be checked.
evidence.scope: The work changes one local runtime setting and verifies the backend, MinIO bucket, and upload persistence together.
evidence.reasoning: The selected MinIO repository writes generated content and metadata keys through one restricted service account.
evidence.verification: A real upload, retrieval, object-name inspection, cleanup, and regression checks are required because this handles private licence files.

workers.scope: read-only review of the existing MinIO repository, service startup, and live-smoke acceptance criteria

execution.coordinator_scope: local configuration activation, project-managed API restart, live persistence verification, and regression checks
execution.recovery: The first restart used system Python, which lacks the locked minio dependency. The second attempt used uv run and started successfully; this was an environment correction, not a model escalation.

passed: MinIO and PostgreSQL containers were already live on loopback-only ports.
The local API restarted through uv run with LICENCEIQ_DOCUMENT_STORAGE_BACKEND=minio and returned health 200.
A generated PNG upload produced exactly two generated MinIO object keys beneath documents/content and documents/metadata, with no filename in either key.
The document remained retrievable with its capability after an API restart; a wrong capability returned 404.
Protected API deletion removed both temporary MinIO objects.
Ruff lint and format checks passed.
not_run: Live OpenAI OCR, extraction, embedding, and question calls were intentionally not invoked by the storage smoke test.
PostgreSQL durable-repository integration remains separate future work; the active MinIO repository stores document bytes and current private metadata objects.
